summary.title: Site Reliability Engineering and the Art of Improvisation
summary.one_liner: Learn how Blameless runs a recurring, low-pressure "gamelan-style" learning session, using group exercises to build SRE intuition and incident-response skills before real outages happen.
takeaways: A weekly, optional, non-meeting 'session' lets engineers practice reasoning about systems outside of incidents.
Exercises include observability walkthroughs, decision requirements tables for on-call decisions, knowledge elicitation, and asking why on-call exists.
A game called 'Spin the Wheel of Expertise' has people show how they find answers or escalate when they don't know.
Practicing routine work together builds the pattern recognition and intuition that help responders during incidents.
Sessions were adapted on the day of a vendor outage into a talk about root certificate authorities and SSL/TLS.
summary.summary: The article is an essay by a Blameless staff member describing a weekly continuous learning session named after the Indonesian gamelan orchestra, where music evolves through group practice. The author lists several formats used in the sessions, such as observability toolset walkthroughs, building decision requirement tables for hard on-call decisions, eliciting team knowledge, discussing the purpose of on-call, and a game for locating expertise. The piece argues that this shared, low-stakes practice (which it calls "the Practice of Practice") builds intuition and collaboration that make incident response more adaptive. It is conceptual and anecdotal rather than a technical how-to, with few concrete implementation details.
